items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: “Yeah I play with Lionel Hampton’s Orchestra.

ctx.x: The Sloan House YMCA. 34th Street between Eighth and Ninth Avenue. Because I had five thousand dollars when I got there. In 1959 five thousand dollars was probably like what, 20 or 30 thousand dollars, because the cost of living was down. I mean Transcontinental Airlines from New York to Chicago by [Inaudible] was 24 dollars and 50 cents. The Four Seasons, the Sheraton, the Waldorf was like 50 dollars a week. You go there now, the occupancy rate is 65 dollars a night. That’s aside from the 300 or 499 dollars, you…

month, which wasn’t bad. Now I’m sure that same place — I go by there sometimes and look at the building — I’m sure that place probably rents for five thousand dollars a month. The same place. So I said I need a phone, so I called the phone company. First thing, “Do you have any references?” I said, “Yeah I play with Lionel Hampton’s Orchestra. They checked it out, telephone, no problem. So the gig worked that way. So now we’re getting ready to go to Wildwood, New Jersey. So Cedar Walton, one of my dearest…

Jones, Frank Foster, Benny Golson, Slide Hampton. You know, certain ones, if I’ve got to play some of that music, get it to me ten weeks ahead of time, you know. So I told Art, I said, “Well you know Art, you know you’re playing all those hard piano parts.” So Benny said, “Don’t worry, Mabern, we’re kind of getting away from that.” Because this time, this would have been the third Jazztet from the original with McCoy Tyner. Then Cedar. Now I’m coming it and that’s the third Jazztet. So sure enough they cut back…
